negatives.observation: Every listed family is present. Nine terms are defined in sequence with no accumulating picture (glossaryAccumulation), each under an identical definition/analogy/'Where it stops'/'In real life'/positioning-line template (templateRepetition). Clueless, the Walkman, the toolbox, the taxi company and Miss Jeeves are ornamental labels that are immediately retracted by the 'Where it stops' clause rather than doing explanatory work (decorativeAnalogy), and their sheer accumulation across consecutive entries is referenceConfetti. Mechanism is asserted, not shown — 'pattern-completion system' and 'learned mathematical transformations' name a process without explaining how it yields the invented commitment the same entry warns about (missingMechanism). The single action offered is a bare instruction to check against originals, unattached to any mechanism that would tell the reader what to check for (genericAction). Tokens are introduced and deferred to a later chapter (jargonBeforeMeaning). Each entry closes by restating its own boundary rather than connecting to the next, so the parts never assemble into one working system (disconnectedSystem), and the promise 'it tells you what to fix' is never redeemed with anything a reader could enjoy or do (joylessInstruction).

negatives.observation: All four required families are present, and this exemplar is genuinely stronger than CQX-BAD-001 — the job-offer decision is concrete and the repair sequence is real. It still fails. The book's purpose is narrowed to fault-location in a pipeline, which cannot carry a whole book (purposeTooNarrow). The Introduction defines AI system, model and context as components before the reader has any felt reason to care, so the machinery precedes the motive (mechanismBeforeMotivation). One comparison then becomes the organising spine of every section, and by the closing map the example has displaced the book's larger promise (workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose). The arrow diagram, the numbered four-question list and the syllabus preview of later chapters are the register of a competent technical explainer rather than a voice with a stake (technicalExplainerVoice). No family from the CQX-BAD-001 set is fairly chargeable here: the prose is continuous and the analogies are absent rather than decorative.

negatives.observation: All six required families are present. The register is measured institutional analysis — allocation decisions, ledgers, frameworks — rather than a story with a point of view (policyMemoVoice, and in the definitional passages technicalExplainerVoice). Three bolded dictionary entries under an explicit 'concepts' heading halt the reporting mid-article (glossaryInterruptsStory). A five-item numbered list converts the ending from news into an assignment (checklistTurnsNewsIntoHomework). Nobody appears: no resident, no meeting, no named town — only percentages and a permit pause, so there is no one for the reader to care about (missingHumanTension). The article narrates its own construction with 'The concepts that make the story legible', the 'useful question is therefore not' pivot and a 'What to keep watching' coda (scaffoldingVisible). The single light line about the cloud keeping its coat is charm, not stake, and cannot carry the absence. The article's factual handling is careful — 'It is not proof of why people changed their minds' — which is why the failure is one of form, not accuracy.

artifactEvidence.excerpt:
Because sounding convincing and checking a fact are different jobs. A language model—the part of an AI system that generates text—can produce a plausible answer without having reliable evidence for it.

Training teaches it patterns in language. Those patterns help it construct a response, but they do not guarantee that a particular date, name or claim is true. A plausible but false statement is often called a hallucination.

An OpenAI research paper gives a revealing example: several models supplied polished answers about a researcher’s dissertation, yet got its title and year wrong. The answer had the shape of a fact; it was still false.

The paper also explains why uncertainty can turn into confident guessing: if training or tests reward a correct guess but give no credit for “I don’t know,” guessing can score better. That helps explain the behaviour; it does not mean every error has the same cause.

When a claim matters, ask for its original source, open it and check whether it supports that exact claim. Asking “Are you sure?” may produce another confident paragraph. What you need is evidence you can inspect.

reverseBrief.humanQuestion: Why does AI sometimes give me a confident answer that is wrong?
reverseBrief.promisedPayoff: Understand why fluent language is not factual verification and inspect an original source.
reverseBrief.centralMentalModel: Training learns patterns in language. Generating a plausible answer does not ensure facts were verified. Rewarding a guess can discourage admitting uncertainty. Inspect original evidence before relying on a claim.
reverseBrief.dailyLifeConnection: A plausible but incorrect dissertation title demonstrates that a polished sentence is not retrieval.
reverseBrief.surfaceJob: A concise reviewed answer to an explicit question, with sources and correction controls.
reverseBrief.desiredReaderFeeling: Able to take one useful step while retaining judgement.

sourceSerializationNote: Exact matching reviewer excerpts retained for validation; all original reviewer wording, including imprecise quotations, is preserved in final-calibration.json.

sourceOfJudgement.transformation: Root mechanically serialized reviewer judgments; no new reviewer findings were invented.

modelExplainBack: Language models generate fluent text from learned patterns, which does not verify any particular fact; scoring that rewards guesses over abstention can push toward confident wrong answers. Check the original source, since re-asking only produces more fluent text.
modelUnseenTransfer: A reader given a confident case citation by an AI opens the citation itself rather than asking the model to confirm it, and finds the case name plausible but the year wrong — the same shape-without-substance failure.
